text.p: Indian parliament on Tuesday approved the 1997/98 (April-March) Finance Bill, the cornerstone of the centre-left's government's budget, local news agencies said.
The upper house, Rajya Sabha approved the bill and it will be sent to President Shankar Dayal Sharma for his signature.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram presented the Finance Bill as part of a broader budget package, slashing taxes and tariffs, on February 28.

The lower house, Lok Sabha approved the Finance Bill on Friday. Last week, Chidambaram accepted minor changes in the budget which would cost the government an extra 1.1 billion rupees ($30.7 million) in the current fiscal year.

The budget has been widely hailed by domestic industry and welcomed by foreign investors but criticised by left parties and main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) for exposing some sectors to more competition.
